name: Mang Den
provinceNote: Kon Tum merged into Quảng Ngãi in the 2025 provincial rearrangement. Signs and addresses in Kon Plông may still say Kon Tum.
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: Pine air at about 1,200 m, mist on Dak Ke lake at first light, and Pa Sy falling through the forest a short ride from your lodge. Sleep in Mang Den when a cool highland night and a waterfall morning are the trip. Sleep in Kon Tum city, about 60 km down Highway 24, only when its wooden church and coffee are the point.
getThere: Fly to Pleiku (PXU), then about 100 km by road
seoTitle: Mang Den travel guide: Pa Sy waterfall and pine air
seoDescription: Sleep among the pines at about 1,200 m in Mang Den: Pa Sy waterfall 9 km out, Dak Ke lake at dawn, and Kon Pring village, 100 km from Pleiku airport.
intro: You wake to pine air on a plateau at about 1,200 m, with a hot cup of local Arabica while the mist lifts off the trees. Get to Dak Ke lake while that mist still sits on the water, or drive out to Pa Sy, where three streams meet and drop through the forest. Seven lakes and three waterfalls are scattered around the town. The afternoon belongs to Kon Pring, a Mơ Nâm village a few kilometres up Highway 24.

Make Mang Den the night if cool air, water in the forest, and a village afternoon are why you came. Da Lat is the other cool plateau, and the larger city if you want one. Kon Tum city, about 60 km southwest on the same highway, is the base for its wooden church and coffee. The mistake is sleeping there and driving up for the day. The pine-and-mist morning only happens if you are already here.

Most people fly into Pleiku, about 100 km away, and come up by hired car or taxi. The last stretch is the pass, a road that snakes over forest, farms, and valleys. Stop at a curve on a clear morning, before the cloud builds. Once you are up, the falls, lakes, and village all sit outside the town strip, so you need wheels: a hired car, a motorbike taxi, a rented motorbike, or your lodge’s driver.

Pa Sy is about 9 km from town, a fall at around 1,500 m in a 25-hectare eco-cultural park with Ro Mam culture displays. You walk down forest stairs to the water. Dak Ke is the best-known lake. Walk the shore, take a canoe out or fish where it is offered, and find the traditional nhà rông beside the water. The smaller Dak Ke waterfall is more remote, with a natural pool you can swim in once you find it. The signs are poor, so ask for the path. Toong Dam is the quiet lake, ringed by old trees.

Kon Pring is one of four community tourism villages in Kon Plông. Come for the communal house, the stilt houses, weaving, rice wine, and gongs, and ask before you photograph inside the nhà rông. Khanh Lam pagoda is the climb: about 200 stone steps up a forested hill to tiered roofs above the trees. In town, the Mang Den church and its Virgin Mary statue make a short stop.

Evenings are quiet, with no bar street. Dinner is grilled chicken with lam rice at a local restaurant or your homestay. Rượu cần, fermented sticky-rice wine drunk through long bamboo straws, comes out around a fire with the gongs. On Saturday and Sunday the market on the pine hill off Hùng Vương fills with highland food. Then sleep early. The best hour here is dawn.
gettingAround: The falls, lakes, and village are all outside the town strip, so plan on wheels. Hire a car or a motorbike taxi, rent a motorbike, or ask your lodge for a driver. Pa Sy is about 9 km out. Kon Pring is on Highway 24, about 3 km from the centre by Mang Den Tourism’s count and about 5 km by Go Vietnam Travel’s and the Vietnam Tourism rural portal’s. Kon Tum city is about 60 km southwest down the same highway, and the town centre sits along Nguyen Hue Street.

stayAreas.name: Mang Den town
stayAreas.summary: Small hotels and homestays along the pine roads, a short ride from the lakes, Pa Sy, and Kon Pring. Forest camping and ethnic homestays are the other ways to sleep up here.

eat: Start with gà nướng cơm lam: grilled chicken with sticky rice cooked in young bamboo and eaten with peanut salt. Then the forest plates: a tray of about 40 indigenous greens and roots, wild banana-flower salad, pork skewers, and fried crickets with a beer. On Saturday and Sunday the pine-hill market off Hùng Vương adds trâu gác bếp, grilled fish and crab, and hạt kơ nia. The full list is on the food guide.
interestsBody: Eat grilled chicken with lam rice, a tray of forest greens, and the weekend market on the pine hill.
Chase the water in the morning: Pa Sy where three streams meet, Dak Ke lake in the mist, and the smaller fall with its pool.
Spend the afternoon at Kon Pring for the communal house and the gongs, then climb the 200 steps to Khanh Lam.

cards.title: Dak Ke Lake
cards.summary: The best-known lake. Walk the shore in the morning mist, take a canoe out or fish where it is offered, and find the nhà rông by the water.

body: Seven lakes and three waterfalls sit around Mang Den. Pa Sy is the fall to plan the morning around: about 9 km from town, at around 1,500 m, where three streams meet. You walk forest stairs down to it. Quảng Ngãi set the gate at 50,000 VND for adults and 25,000 VND for children from 30 May 2026, under Resolution 52/2026/NQ-HĐND. Older listings, including Việt Úc Tourist’s, still show the earlier 20,000 VND.

Dak Ke lake is a short drive from town. Go early, when the water is still and the plateau is known for cloud at dawn. Canoeing and fishing are offered, and a traditional nhà rông stands on the shore. The smaller Dak Ke waterfall is more remote. Once you reach it, you can swim in the pool. The signs are poor, so ask in town for the path. Toong Dam is the quiet lake, ringed by old trees.
Come in on the pass if you can do it in daylight. The road snakes over forest, farms, and valleys, and a clear morning shows the valleys before the cloud builds.

cards.title: Kon Pring village
cards.summary: A Mơ Nâm village on Highway 24. See the nhà rông, the stilt houses, and the gongs, and give it at least an hour. Open 05:00–21:00.

body: Kon Pring is one of four community tourism villages in Kon Plông, a few kilometres up Highway 24 from town. The tall roof of the nhà rông rises over the fields, with stilt houses under the pine behind. Give it at least an hour. The gate is open 05:00–21:00. Ask before you photograph inside the communal house.

Gongs and xoang dancing, weaving, and rice wine are part of a visit. They run on no fixed weekly schedule, so ask that morning. Stay in a homestay if you want the village after dark and a family meal.

Khanh Lam pagoda sits on a forested hill above town. Climb about 200 stone steps to the tiered roofs above the trees. Back in town, the Mang Den church and its Virgin Mary statue are a short stop on the way to dinner.

season.label: Cool year-round
season.note: Pack a layer in any month: the air averages about 16–20 °C. Việt Úc Tourist points to October–December for the easiest Pa Sy road, and other travel blogs give a broader dry window. After heavy rain, ask your lodge whether the road and the forest stairs are open. The cultural festival ran 27–30 November in 2023. Confirm this year’s dates before you plan around it.

faqs.q: Is Mang Den part of Kon Tum city?
faqs.a: No. It is a plateau town in Kon Plông, about 60 km northeast of Kon Tum city on Highway 24. Kon Tum province merged into Quảng Ngãi in 2025, so you will see both names. Sleep in Mang Den when the pine night is the point.

faqs.q: What does Pa Sy waterfall cost?
faqs.a: Quảng Ngãi set the gate at 50,000 VND for adults and 25,000 VND for children from 30 May 2026, under Resolution 52/2026/NQ-HĐND. Older listings, including Việt Úc Tourist’s, still show the earlier 20,000 VND. Pay the price on the board at the counter.

faqs.q: How do I get to Mang Den?
faqs.a: There is no airport in town. Fly to Pleiku, about 100 km away, and come up by hired car or taxi. From Kon Tum city it is about 60 km on Highway 24. The last stretch is the pass, so arrive in daylight if you can.

faqs.q: Is there nightlife in Mang Den?
faqs.a: Not a bar street. The evening is a grilled-chicken-and-lam-rice dinner at a local restaurant or your homestay, and rượu cần around a fire when the gongs come out. Most people sleep early for the dawn mist.

faqs.q: When is the Mang Den cultural festival?
faqs.a: The 2023 edition ran 27–30 November in Mang Den town, with a caravan, a food contest, and a music show. The Mang Den Ultra Trail opened on 20 February in 2025. Confirm this year’s dates for both before you plan around them.
